record.original_question: Is the geometrical (rectilinear) crossing number of every complete bipartite graph equal to its ordinary crossing number?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.6 The geometrical crossing number of the complete bipartite graph is equal to its crossing number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph G, define the crossing number cr(G) to be the minimum number of pairwise crossings of edges over all drawings of G in the plane in which edges are continuous arcs that meet only at common endpoints or at transverse crossings (and no three edges share a crossing point). Define the rectilinear (geometric) crossing number cr̄(G) to be the minimum number of pairwise crossings over all drawings of G in the plane in which the vertices are points in general position and every edge is drawn as the straight line segment joining its endpoints.

For positive integers m, n, let K_{m,n} denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes m and n.

Question: Is it true that cr̄(K_{m,n}) = cr(K_{m,n}) for every pair of positive integers m, n?
artifact.status_search_result: The equality of the rectilinear and ordinary crossing numbers for all complete bipartite graphs K_{m,n} is a long-standing conjecture closely tied to Zarankiewicz's conjecture. Surveys on crossing numbers and recent papers establishing bounds (e.g., cr̄(K_{n,n}) ≥ 0.987·Z(n,n) + o(n^4)) treat it as open; neither the rectilinear nor the ordinary crossing number of K_{m,n} is known in general, and no proof of their equality is known.

status_evidence.title: The Graph Crossing Number and its Variants: A Survey (Schaefer)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses conjectures relating rectilinear and ordinary crossing numbers, including the conjecture cr̄(K_{m,n}) = cr(K_{m,n}).
status_evidence.claim: The equality cr̄(K_{m,n}) = cr(K_{m,n}) is listed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The Rectilinear Crossing Number of K_n: Closing In (Or Are We?)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys what is known about rectilinear crossing numbers; the bipartite analogue and its relation to cr(K_{m,n}) remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: No proof that the rectilinear and ordinary crossing numbers of K_{m,n} are equal is known.

status_evidence.title: On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work giving lower bounds for cr̄(K_{n,n}), still bounded away from the conjectured Zarankiewicz value.
status_evidence.claim: Rectilinear crossing number of K_{n,n} is not yet determined and equality with cr(K_{n,n}) is open.
